title: US Revokes Over 600 Visas as Birth Tourism Crackdown Widens to Three Continents
excerpt: American embassies in Europe, West Africa, and North Africa have dismantled organized networks that helped foreign nationals travel to the US to give birth and secure citizenship for their children.
body:
• US embassies across Europe, West Africa, and North Africa have revoked more than 600 visas linked to organized birth tourism schemes.
  • A European embassy identified over 400 suspected cases since 2024, traced to at least six coaching companies.
  • President Trump signed executive orders on August 7 expanding the definition of those ineligible for birthright citizenship and formally banning birth tourism.
  • Several individuals linked to the networks have been permanently banned from entering the United States.

The United States has dismantled multiple international birth tourism networks and revoked more than 600 visas across Europe, West Africa, and North Africa, as the Trump administration escalates enforcement against what it calls abuse of the American citizenship system.

The State Department disclosed that US embassies in three regions uncovered organized networks that helped foreign nationals obtain visitor visas primarily to give birth in the United States and secure citizenship for their children.

How the Networks Operated

A US embassy in Europe identified more than 400 suspected birth tourism cases since 2024, tracing them to at least six companies. These firms coached applicants on visa interview responses, arranged housing in the US, and coordinated delivery plans. The visas were revoked, and several individuals received permanent travel bans.

In West Africa, investigators uncovered a network involving more than 100 foreign nationals who allegedly used fraudulent documents and visa "fixers" to obtain travel documents under false pretenses. A separate North African operation led to more than 100 additional visa revocations.

"We shut it down, revoked their visas, and permanently banned several fraudsters from travelling to the United States ever again."

— US State Department

Executive Orders Tighten the Framework

The visa revocations come alongside executive orders signed by President Trump on August 7 that formally ban birth tourism and expand the definitions of people ineligible for birthright citizenship. The orders follow the Supreme Court's June 30 ruling that struck down Trump's earlier, broader attempt to restrict birthright citizenship as unconstitutional.

"That practice of birth tourism is, as of the signing of this order, hereby banned. What that means is that no one in the world is anymore allowed to obtain a visa for this fraudulent purpose," White House aide Stephen Miller said during the signing ceremony.

The Center for Immigration Studies estimated that between 20,000 and 25,000 mothers came to the US for birth tourism annually in the 2016-2017 period. While the practice has historically been associated with travelers from China and Russia, the latest enforcement actions reveal its spread to Africa and parts of Europe.

Implications for Visa Applicants

The crackdown signals tighter scrutiny of visitor visa applications from pregnant travelers worldwide. While the current enforcement has targeted organized networks in Europe and Africa, immigration attorneys say consular officers are now more likely to question the travel intentions of any visa applicant who appears to be in the later stages of pregnancy, regardless of nationality. For Indian diaspora families planning visits to the US, the shifting enforcement posture adds another layer of uncertainty to an already complex visa landscape.
